headline: Majors hold above 200-days with RSI stretched; whales accumulating onto exchanges as ETF outflow reshapes the bid.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and all report MACD above signal line, but no golden cross has formed on any of them. This is a regime where the trend is up and momentum is aligned with it, yet the move lacks the formal confirmation that would signal a structural shift. Bitcoin sits 37 percent below its 12-month high of $124,740, while Ethereum and Solana are down 47.6 and 57.4 percent respectively from their 12-month peaks. The 90-day ranges show real space between price and the extremes, Bitcoin trading from $58,566 to $80,268 and Solana from $62.18 to $109.18, so the recent rallies are not taking out new bars. One asset stands apart: Dogecoin trades below its 200-day line despite a MACD cross above signal, a technical breach that separates it from the six others. Cardano has already turned its MACD back below signal, the only major to show that reversal, and it sits 78.2 percent below its 12-month high, the weakest performer in the set.

RSI-14 readings are elevated across the board. Bitcoin at 72.1, Ethereum at 71.1, and Solana at 75.2 all sit in or near overbought territory (70 and above), while Bitcoin and Ethereum have also run 21 and 32 percent respectively over the past 30 days. This is momentum, not a regime problem. In shorter windows, though, tension emerges: Solana is down 0.1 percent on the day while up 20.3 percent on the week, and Dogecoin is flat on the day while up 6.0 percent on the week. These divergences between the very short and the intermediate term suggest the rallies are tiring into session closes even as the broader uptrend persists. Cardano's RSI sits at 53.5 and its MACD has already rolled under signal, the earliest sign of momentum failure in the cohort.

Derivatives positioning reveals two distinct stories. Bitcoin and Ethereum carry positive funding, 8.4 and 7.0 percent annualized respectively, with long-short ratios of 1.17 and 1.36, meaning the crowd is long and paying to hold it. Solana has turned negative, funding at minus 1.9 percent annualized with a 1.66 long-short ratio, a state where holders are paying to short instead of long, even though more accounts are long than short. This is a tension: crowded longs that are losing the bid for money. Bitcoin's open interest sits at $2.2 billion, Ethereum at $1.55 billion, and Solana at $339 million. Over the prior 22 to 23 hours, shorts were liquidated far more than longs, Bitcoin saw $1.89 million in short liquidations against $18,879 in long liquidations, Ethereum saw $1.53 million in short liquidations against $40,929 in longs. Solana bucked the pattern, with $635,901 in short liquidations but $476,644 in long liquidations. Dogecoin funding is running hot at 11.0 percent annualized with a 4.02 long-short ratio, the most skewed positioning among the five, a setup where retail conviction is highest and the least stable.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours show $219.6 million moving onto exchanges, led by Bitcoin. The Bitcoin flows carried $164.7 million net onto exchanges, with the largest single movements into Coinbase at $184.9 million and two separate Kraken moves at $158.7 and $157.8 million. In the same window, $158.2 million moved off Kraken and $149.2 million off Coinbase, showing internal liquidity churn rather than a pure directional exodus. The weekly picture, though, is clearer: the four weeks through Aug 30 saw three consecutive weeks of net flows onto exchanges, totaling $2.23 billion over weeks ending Aug 16, Aug 23, and Aug 30. Week ending Aug 9 was the lone exception, $67 million off exchanges. This is supply hitting the bid. Ethereum shows $54.9 million net onto exchanges in the 48-hour window and ten consecutive days of same-direction inflow. Stablecoin float sits at $309.8 billion, up 1.36 percent over 30 days, ample dry powder but not aggressively accumulating.

The ETF flows paint a split picture. Bitcoin saw a $201.9 million outflow on 28 Aug, yet the last five sessions cumulated to $924.5 million inflow, a contradiction that names a single day of selling into a broader bid. Ethereum reported $102.1 million inflow on 28 Aug and ten consecutive days of same-direction flows, cumulating $815.7 million over five sessions. The Fear and Greed gauge sits at 69 (Greed), near the high of its 30-day range at 74, showing the crowd is bullish. Total market cap fell 2.24 percent on the day despite price gains in most majors, suggesting the declines elsewhere outweighed the rallies. Bitcoin dominance held at 59.5 percent. The setup is one where the crowd is greedy and positioned long, whales are accumulating coins onto exchanges at scale, momentum is elevated and aligned with trend, yet the very short-term price action is turning sideways to down even as the 200-day frame holds. Watch whether Bitcoin can reclaim $80,000 and hold it; watch whether Solana's negative funding reverts back to positive; watch whether the weekly whale flows reverse off exchanges and whether stablecoin float starts to decline materially.

Network conditions show Bitcoin transaction fees at 1 sat per byte for both fastest and hourly confirmation, low friction for chain movement. Difficulty is expected to retarget up 0.3 percent in 935 blocks, a minor adjustment. The tape does not show panic or distress. It shows elevated positioning, whales moving coins onto the margin, and the crowd feeling good. The question is whether the RSI stretch and the late-day weakness in Solana and Dogecoin despite weekly strength signal the beginning of a rest within the trend or the prelude to a reversal.
